citations.anchor: refuses a tool the actor lacks the permission for
citations.why: Calls `registry.call` for a tool the context lacks the permission for and asserts both a ForbiddenException and that the handler never ran, so the gate is provably in `call()` and provably before dispatch. (The 'no handler checks its own requires' half is a universal negative over every provider in the repo and is not pinned.)

citations.anchor: refuses a tool a hidden-from-list actor invokes by name
citations.why: Asserts `visibleTo` returns nothing for the actor AND that naming the tool anyway is still refused — exactly the claim that the filter is a nicety and `call()` is the boundary.

citations.anchor: requires EVERY permission a tool declares
citations.why: A tool declaring two permissions is refused for an actor holding one and runs for an actor holding both, so an any-of check would fail the first assertion. (Exact-string matching of a key is only pinned indirectly, by the boot check on an unknown `requires` value.)

citations.anchor: refuses a write tool a read token invokes by name
citations.why: The token is minted through the real API by an admin user and carries that user in `userId`; naming `content_create` is still refused with `forbidden`, so the issuing user's role provably plays no part in authorization.

citations.anchor: derives permissions from the token scope, not the minting user
citations.why: The actor half: permissions come from the scope, `actor.id` is the token, and `actor.userId` carries the minting user purely as attribution.

citations.anchor: offers a tool that names no surfaces to both
citations.why: A tool with no `surfaces` field is asserted present in both `forSurface('mcp')` and `forSurface('copilot')`.

citations.anchor: refuses to boot on an empty surfaces array
citations.why: The second clause: `onApplicationBootstrap` throws 'offered to neither consumer' on `surfaces: []`, so such a tool cannot ship.

citations.anchor: refuses to dispatch a tool the calling surface was never offered
citations.why: A copilot-only tool called on the `mcp` surface rejects with NotFoundException (not Forbidden) and the handler never runs — the surface narrowing is applied inside `call()`.

citations.anchor: stamps the dispatching surface on the handler
citations.why: The context handed to `call` carries no surface (createToolContext sets none), yet the handler observes `surface === 'mcp'`, so it is stamped by the registry at dispatch and cannot be asserted by the caller.

citations.anchor: 404s an unknown tool, distinctly from a refusal
citations.why: An unknown name throws NotFoundException while the sibling authorization cases throw ForbiddenException, so conflating the two answers fails one of them. (That the refusal message names the keys is not asserted anywhere.)

citations.anchor: reports an unknown tool as not_found
citations.why: The same distinction survives to the wire: an unknown name comes back `not_found` where a permission refusal in the same suite comes back `forbidden`.

citations.anchor: 404s an ungranted type exactly like an unknown one
citations.why: The MCP half, asserted side by side: `content_type_get` on an ungranted type and on a non-existent type both answer `not_found`.

citations.anchor: refuses a content type the workspace was not granted
citations.why: The copilot half: an ungranted type is refused with the 'Unknown content type' wording a non-existent type gets, rather than anything that would confirm the type exists.

citations.anchor: refuses on permissions before it looks at the arguments
citations.why: An unauthorized caller sending arguments the schema rejects gets ForbiddenException, not the UnprocessableEntityException the same arguments produce when authorized.

citations.anchor: treats missing arguments as an empty object
citations.why: `registry.call(name, undefined, …)` resolves, so the defaulting is done by the registry itself rather than by either consumer's `?? {}`.

citations.anchor: hides a resource the actor lacks the permission for
citations.why: The listing half: `resources()` returns [] for an actor missing the resource's declared `requires`.

citations.anchor: refuses to read it even when the uri is named directly
citations.why: The read half: `readResource` on the same URI throws ForbiddenException before any provider is asked for the bytes.

citations.anchor: refuses to boot when two providers claim one name
citations.why: The duplicate-name clause: `onApplicationBootstrap` (the hook Nest runs inside app.init()) throws naming the duplicate.

citations.anchor: refuses to boot on a name that is not snake_case
citations.why: The name-pattern clause: a padded, mixed-case name aborts boot.

citations.anchor: refuses to boot on a requires the deployment does not define
citations.why: The unknown-permission clause: a `requires` entry outside PERMISSION_KEYS aborts boot.

citations.anchor: refuses to boot on an inputSchema that is not an object schema
citations.why: The inputSchema clause: `{ type: 'string' }` aborts boot ('tool arguments are always an object').

citations.anchor: reports every problem at once, not just the first
citations.why: The 'every problem reported at once' clause: a catalogue broken in two ways throws a message asserted to name both.

citations.anchor: ignores a provider instance registered twice
citations.why: The idempotence clause: the same provider instance registered twice yields one copy of its tools and still boots.

citations.anchor: throws when two providers claim the same tool name
citations.why: The second clause: two *different* providers claiming one name still make `all()` throw rather than one silently winning.

citations.anchor: shows one shared tool to both surfaces of one running app
citations.why: In one booted app, the same tools registered once are asserted visible over MCP `tools/list` and in the copilot run's offer — which can only hold if both consumers resolved the same ToolRegistry instance.

citations.anchor: does nothing when no registry is bound
citations.why: A capability plugin's provider constructed with no registry runs `onModuleInit` without throwing, pinning the `@Optional()` contract. (The other clause — a deployment with *both* consumers off booting — is exercised by no test: the e2e turns off one at a time.)

citations.anchor: leaves the copilot a full catalogue
citations.why: With `mcpEnabled: false` the MCP route 404s while a copilot run is still offered the registry's tools, so the switch removed only the routes.

citations.anchor: leaves the MCP endpoint a full catalogue
citations.why: The symmetric half: with the copilot disabled, `tools/list` over MCP still carries the content and shared tools.

citations.anchor: reports a non-HTTP error as an opaque internal error
citations.why: A bare Error carrying a connection string becomes `{500, internal_error, 'The tool failed unexpectedly…'}` and the serialized result is asserted not to contain 'ECONNREFUSED'. (That the stack reaches only the log is not asserted.)

citations.anchor: carries per-field validation issues through verbatim
citations.why: A 422 carrying `issues` is flattened with the identical array under the identical `issues` key, so any reshaping or renaming fails the toEqual.

citations.anchor: keeps the first declaration of a name and withholds the shadow
citations.why: `resolveCapabilityProfile` — the only place in the repo that implements this rule — is asserted to offer the first declaration and to report the repeat in `withheld` with reason 'duplicate-name'.

tools:I-09.reason: A universal coding rule over every tool handler in seven other packages ('never a check, a filter, or a disclosed field keyed on surface'). No harness can assert the absence of such a branch; a test can only sample individual tools, and the one shared tool that does render per surface is already exercised for its presentation difference (apps/server-e2e/src/server/mcp/mcp.spec.ts 'gives an MCP caller the bearer-fetchable download path' and apps/server-e2e/src/server/copilot/copilot-read-catalogue.spec.ts 'carries a download path the asking user's browser can follow'). Enforcement is review + the ToolContext.surface JSDoc (packages/tools/server/src/lib/tool.ts:66-85).

tools:I-25.reason: Contradicted as written. packages/tools/server/src/lib/tool.ts:132 declares `export type ToolSurface = 'mcp' | 'copilot'` — a type that names MCP; packages/tools/server/src/lib/tool-error.ts:25 is `const logger = new Logger('McpTools')` (the dossier's own §17 divergence table flags this line); and packages/tools/server/src/lib/tool-registry.ts:205-225 signals refusals with Nest HTTP exceptions (NotFoundException / ForbiddenException / UnprocessableEntityException) while packages/tools/server/src/lib/tool-error.ts:6 documents ToolError.status as an 'HTTP-ish status'. The intended, defensible statement — no JSON-RPC or transport type crosses the contract, and no dependency on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk — is the separate I-24.
